answer: fiscal_quarter is a PL/SQL function that lives only in the Oracle schema. Nothing created it in PostgreSQL, so the translated query fails with 'function does not exist'. Either port the function to PL/pgSQL, or drop the call and write EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM d_date) directly in the query.
The translation fails because PostgreSQL uses a different date format than Oracle. Set DateStyle to ISO and it will work.
The function was never migrated to the target, which is why the query fails there.

A rule-based tool may simply remove the (+) marker. The join then becomes an inner join: rows without a match disappear, the query still runs, and no error tells you. Rewrite it as an explicit LEFT JOIN and run both versions against the same data to confirm the row sets agree.
The (+) syntax is deprecated and slow. A translator might produce a query that takes longer on PostgreSQL, so check the execution plan.
The marker can be dropped, turning the outer join into an inner join that silently loses unmatched rows. Use LEFT JOIN instead.
